svg.title: The Nazi Police State, Pre-War Concentration Camps & Church Opposition (1933–39)
svg.desc: Historical GIS atlas map of the Nazi Police State inside 1933–39 pre-war Reich borders, charting Himmler’s SS, Heydrich’s SD and Gestapo HQ, the People’s Court in Berlin, pre-war SS concentration camps (Dachau, Sachsenhausen, Buchenwald, Flossenbürg, Ravensbrück, Esterwegen, Lichtenburg), and Confessing and Catholic Church opposition at Barmen, Berlin-Dahlem, and Münster.

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · PAPER 3 (OPTION 31) · KT3.2: POLICE STATE & CHURCHES
The Nazi Police State, Pre-War Concentration Camps & Church Opposition (1933–39)
Himmler’s SS (240,000 men), Heydrich’s SD & Gestapo (32,000 agents aided by civilian informers), and Freisler’s People’s Court enforced terror
via protective custody in pre-war SS camps (Dachau 1933, Sachsenhausen 1936, Buchenwald 1937), silencing Confessing Church & Catholic dissent.
